files.title: Digital Omnibus on data: GDPR, ePrivacy, Data Act, NIS2
files.status: The Commission proposed it on 19 November 2025. Member States are close to a Council position (EDRi letter, 18 September 2026). Parliament's position is still being built in joint ITRE-LIBE work and will take months. Open fights: personal data and pseudonymisation, AI training on personal data, and whether cookie rules move into the GDPR or stay in ePrivacy.

files.title: Digital Fairness Act (and a possible EU social media minimum age)
files.status: The Commission is on track to present the proposal in Q4 2026. Expected themes: dark patterns, addictive design, influencer marketing, unfair personalisation and minors. A bloc-wide social media minimum age may come alongside or inside it. Member States are moving first, for example Denmark's consultation on a minimum age of 15 launched 7 September 2026.

files.title: Technology Sovereignty Package: Chips Act 2.0 and Cloud and AI Development Act
files.status: Both proposals went to Parliament and Council in May–June 2026 (sources differ on the exact date). The Chips Act 2.0 Council working party resumed talks on 2 September 2026. The CADA aims to triple EU data-centre capacity within five to seven years and creates a framework to assess cloud and AI sovereignty, which is the most contested element.

files.title: AI Act implementation after the Digital Omnibus on AI
files.status: The Digital Omnibus on AI entered into force on 27 July 2026. Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 and Annex I from 2 August 2028. Providers of generative AI already on the market have until 2 December 2026 for labelling measures. The live issues are standards, AI Office enforcement and national authority designation.
